[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcdaStudy Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The study module contains features relating to the study of the Bible, sermons, and other learning material.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bibleRdrHd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcd6Bible Reader", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bibleRdr01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Bible page shows the Bible one chapter at a time. Choose a translation, a book and a chapter at the top of the page, and click Next or Previous to turn the page. Each chapter has its own address, such as /app/bible/BSB/JHN/3, so you can bookmark it or send it to someone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bibleRdr02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The reader opens your church's Default Bible Translation, set on the Church form. Members and visitors read the Bible on the website at /bible, which members also reach from the portal menu. Visitors see only the free translations. Members who are signed in also see the translations your church imported.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bibleTrnHd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\ude1aTranslations", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bibleTrn01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Bible Translation holds the whole text of one translation of the Bible. Every Bible reference in the app is read in a translation: in the Bible reader, on bulletins, on Scripture slides and in Bible Memory.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bibleTrn02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding a translation, note the following:
- The Abbreviation, such as ESV, names the translation throughout the app.
- For a free translation, choose Free Use Bible API as the Text Source and type its id from the Free Use Bible API list, such as BSB or eng_kjv. After you save, its text downloads by itself within a minute or two, and the Status changes from Downloading to Ready. If the download fails, check the id and click Download Again.
- For a translation that is not free, such as the NIV, ESV or NLT, choose User Import and attach a copy of its text that your church is licensed to use: a CSV file with the columns book, chapter, verse and text, one verse to a row. Attach it as a private file.
- An imported text is shown only to people who are signed in, never to website visitors, because it may be under copyright.
- By default, only users with the 'Church Manager' role can add or change translations.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bibleTrn03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The app comes with common English translations. The default one (the BSB) downloads its text when the app is installed. Each other free translation (the KJV, WEB, ASV, BBE and Douay-Rheims) downloads itself the first time anyone opens it, so installing does not fetch text nobody reads. The rest wait with the Status 'No Text' until your church imports its own copy.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bibleRefHd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udd16Bible References", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bibleRef01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Wherever the app asks for a Bible reference, type it the way you would write it, such as John 3:16, rom 8:28-30 or Psalm 23. Separate several passages with a semicolon: Romans 3:23; Ephesians 2:8-9. You type references for the Church Verse on the Church form, the Verse of the Week on a Bulletin, the Bible References of a Belief, Scripture slides in a Sermon, and Bible Memory passages.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bibleRef02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you save, note the following:
- The reference is written out in full, such as Romans 8:28-30, but kept as you typed it: several passages stay in the order you listed them, and a whole chapter stays a chapter, so Psalm 23 stays Psalms 23 rather than becoming Psalms 23:1-6.
- A reference the app cannot read is refused, so check the book name and the chapter and verse numbers.
- Books outside the 66 books of the Bible, such as Tobit, are not supported yet.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "on_WLsvqX-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\udde0Bible Memory", "col": 12}}, {"id": "I5mqlBgKcb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Bible Memory feature in the portal provides an interface for users to memorize Scripture. Each person has a personalized list  which tracked as Bible Memory Items, and every completed practice run is logged as a Memory Session.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iSZC5KaXPr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Memorizing on the Portal", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zupDTNZ5oy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "From the portal menu, click \"Bible Memory\"

Create a Memory Goal:
- Click + Add passage, type a passage such as John 3:16-18, choose a translation, and click Add to my list. Only translations whose text is ready are offered.
- Select \"Hide memorized\" to filter out already memorized verses.

Memory Modes:
- Use \"Blur\" mode to become familiarize with the reference text.
    - Click \"+ Increase Blur\" to blur out a few words at a time.
    - When finished, click \"Done\" to increase memory progress by 5% (99% Maximum - 'Type' mode must be used to increase memorization % to 100.
- Use the \"Type\" mode to type the first letter of each word.
    - A perfect run (zero mistakes) awards 50% progress and increments the \"perfect runs\" counter
    - Under three mistakes awards 10% toward the memorization progress.
    - Mistakes subtract 2% progress for each mistake.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10MemPortal", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Passages from a group. If a manager assigned passages to you through a group, choose the group at the top of the Bible Memory page to see only those passages. Choose All groups to see all of your passages again.
Reveal. In Blur mode, press and hold the eyes button to see all words. When you let go, the words that you blurred are blurred again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bpb884l7Wv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Assigning Passages for Memorization", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cjiqQMh3Q4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Managers can add a passage to one or more users' memory lists. This is useful for weekly memory verses or small-group assignments.

From the Bible Memory Item list:
1. Click 'Assign a Passage'.
2. Type the passage and choose its translation.
3. Pick a Group, a User, or both. When a Group is chosen, everyone in the group who has a portal login is assigned the passage.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0xfQDjLm43", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Notes on assignment:
- You can assign a passage only in a translation you can read, and only to people of your own churches.
- Each assignment creates a Bible Memory Item stamped with Assigned By, which shows up under the reference on the recipient's Bible Memory list.
- If a passage is already in the user's list in that translation, the assignment is skipped.
- When assigning to a Group, if the Person record has no linked 'Portal User' listed, a follow-up dialog will be displayed showing which persons don't have user accounts yet.
- When assigning to a User, if a person is not available, that means the person has not been invited to the portal yet and doesn't have a linked User account (i.e. they don't have an account to log into the portal).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10MemGroup", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Group assignments. When you assign a passage to a Group, each item that the assignment adds for a member of the group keeps the group. A member who already has the passage keeps the item that they have, and that item gets no group. A user that you name in User and who is not a member of the group gets no group. You cannot set or change the group of an item by hand. Only a group assignment sets it. When you delete a group, its members keep their passages, and the passages show no group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "aM5F05OfNT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Reporting", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sq843t9BJj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Bible Memory report lists memory progress, with filters for Memorized (Yes, No or all), a User and a Group. To see the progress of a group:
1. Open the Bible Memory report.
2. In Group, select the group.
3. To see all passages, clear Memorized.
The Group filter shows only the passages that the group assignment added. A member who had the passage before the assignment does not show in the group. To see that member, clear Group and select the user. If you cannot open the group, the report shows an error.
If your user is limited to some churches, the report shows only the passages of users whose person record is in those churches. Otherwise it shows all passages, also the passages of users with no person record.
The References Memorized card on the Study workspace tracks total memorizations over time.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "W_SrD0oSAz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcddSermons", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nbEHeWXsAp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Sermon is a collection of slides that can be presented at a church event. Each sermon has a title, an optional 'Prepared By' field linking to a Person, and optional notes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iak3lFqr80", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a sermon, note the following:
- Add slides to the 'Slides' table to build your sermon content. Each slide shows a document, such as a Belief or a Song, or a passage of Scripture.
- For a Scripture slide, leave the Slide Type empty and type the passage in Scripture, such as Psalm 23. Choose a translation, or leave it blank for your church's default. The slide shows the verses in that translation. On the public website, a translation your church imported shows its reference only.
- For a document slide, you can select which fields from the linked document to show on the slide.
  - You may choose a field to use as the slide title by checking the 'Title' box.
  - If no fields are selected, the slide will show the linked document's name as the title. A Song slide with no fields selected shows each slide of the song, then a slide with its copyright and CCLI numbers. Visitors who are not signed in see a song only when Public Domain is ticked on it.
- The 'Presentation History' table tracks when and where the sermon has been presented, who presented it, and optionally includes a recording of the sermon.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IdqC6ue2s5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Presenting a Sermon", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O5YqX1I5FA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To present a sermon, click the 'Present' button on the sermon document:
- Use the arrow keys, or spacebar to navigate between slides.
- Press Escape or click the `X` button to exit the presentation.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p_rUjtXqFB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example Workflow", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VseMD6jUIg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. The Pastor creates a new Sermon and adds Scripture slides and slides showing Beliefs, Songs, etc.
2. He adds per-slide notes to show in the presentation, and general sermon notes. The general notes are not presented, but they show on the website when the sermon is published.
3. On Sunday, he clicks 'Present' to display the sermon.
4. After the service, a row is added to 'Presentation History' table with the date, presenter, location, and optionally an audio/video recording of the sermon.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hndHeading01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u270d\ufe0fSermon Handouts", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hndIntro0001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Sermon Handout is a fill-in-the-blank outline of a sermon for listeners. It is printed as the sermon notes insert of a Bulletin whose function has the sermon on its schedule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hndCreate001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To create a handout, open the sermon and choose 'Create -> Create Handout'. The handout starts as a copy of the sermon's notes and is linked from the sermon's 'Handout' field.
- Wrap a word or phrase in square brackets, like [grace], to print it as a blank for listeners to fill in. The bracketed text stays visible in the handout itself, so it doubles as the answer key.
- Keep the handout to about half a page; the bulletin insert has fixed space.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10SrmWebH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\udf10Sermons on the Website", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10SrmWeb01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each published sermon has its own page on the website, at /sermon/ followed by the name of the sermon. Anyone with the link can open it. On the Sermons page, the title of each sermon opens its page. The sermon page shows the sermon date, the Scripture passage, the preacher, the series, the video, the audio recording and the notes. The notes of a published sermon are public: the Sermons page, the home page and the sermon page show them. If the sermon belongs to a church that is not published, its page shows \"Page not found\".", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10SrmWeb02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On the Sermon form, note the following:
1. Sermon Date is the date when the sermon was first preached. If you leave it empty, Churchit sets it from the earliest date in Presentation History.
2. Scripture is the passage of the sermon, such as John 3:16-21. Separate passages with a semicolon. Churchit tidies the reference when you save.
3. Video Link is an https link to the video of the sermon. A video on Let's Church, YouTube or PeerTube plays on the sermon page. Any other link shows as a Watch the video link. A link that does not start with https:// cannot be saved.
4. When you change the title of a published sermon, the address of its page changes too. Churchit adds a redirect from the old address to the new one, so old links keep working. You find these redirects in Website Settings under Route Redirects. A sermon that is not published gets no redirect.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10SrmWeb03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Search. The Sermons page shows the newest sermons first, by Sermon Date. Type part of a title or a passage, such as John, in the search box and click Search. Click Show all to see all sermons again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10SrmWeb04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Series images. A published Sermon Series shows its Series Image at the top of its card on the Sermons page. The image is a public file. An image that you attached before this change is private and does not show. Remove it from the series and attach it again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10SrmWeb05", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Notes for listeners. When a sermon has a Handout, the sermon page shows the handout as Sermon Notes in place of the sermon notes. Each word in [square brackets] becomes an empty box that the listener fills in. The bracketed words do not show on the sermon page. Below the outline is a My Notes box. What a listener types stays in the browser on their own device, and Churchit does not receive it. Print prints only the notes. Copy puts the filled outline and the notes on the clipboard.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10PodH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\udfa7Sermon Podcast", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10Pod01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The website has a podcast feed of your sermons at /podcast.xml. Podcast apps such as Apple Podcasts, Spotify and AntennaPod read this feed. The Sermons page has a Subscribe to the podcast link to it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10Pod02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The feed shows each published sermon that has public audio. When a sermon has no audio of its own, the feed uses the recording of its newest presentation in Presentation History, with the date of that presentation. When you publish a sermon, Churchit makes its audio and each presentation recording public. When you unpublish it, Churchit makes them private again. A recording that you added before this change becomes public the next time you save the published sermon.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r10Pod03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The feed uses the name, About, Image and Email of the Church. Use a square image of 1400 to 3000 pixels, because Apple Podcasts refuses a smaller one, and attach it as a public file. If the image is private, the feed shows the Churchit icon. With more than one church, each church has its own feed, and the feed of a church also shows the sermons that are shared with all churches. To add the podcast to Apple Podcasts or Spotify, copy the address of the Subscribe link and add it in Apple Podcasts Connect or Spotify for Creators.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r11PodImage", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Make the Church image public. When you attach the image to the Image of the Church, clear Private in the upload window before you click Upload. An image that is already attached is usually private. To make the image public, open the File list, open the image by its file name, clear Is Private and save. The Church then uses the public file. Anyone who has the link to a public file can open it. If only System Managers can upload public files on your site, ask a System Manager.", "col": 12}}]
